ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all founding parties, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, directors and signatories against: (i) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (ii) UN Security Council sanctions regimes; (iii) the French domestic asset-freeze list (Fichier Gelsan, Direction générale du Trésor); and (iv) OFAC sanctions lists as prudent cross-border practice. Domestic and foreign PEPs, their family members and close associates are subject to enhanced due diligence under Article L.561-10-2 of the French Monetary and Financial Code. For this medium-risk sodium-ion battery cell manufacturer, source-of-funds evidence must be obtained for any capital contribution and every SWIFT wire or Letter of Credit must carry complete originator and beneficiary data under applicable EU transfer-of-funds regulations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: INPI Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) for corporate filings; Infogreffe and the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) for pre-clearance search and Kbis verification.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A SARL corporate name must be registered in Latin alphabetic characters, including permitted French diacritics. Non-Latin script names must be transliterated into Latin characters for all official filings. The chosen name must include the legal-form mention 'SARL' or 'Société à responsabilité limitée' in the company's legal name. Under the Loi Toubon, French must be used in all mandatory statutory disclosures and French-language versions of documents prevail for official purposes.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: There is no statutory extension of the 90-day name pre-clearance window; after expiration the name search must be renewed. If the Guichet Unique or the competent Registry refuses a proposed name because it is identical or confusingly similar to an existing RCS name or protected corporate/trade name, the applicant may: (1) submit a new application with an amended name; (2) seek urgent summary relief before the President of the competent commercial court (référé) to contest an arbitrary registry refusal; or (3) where third-party intellectual property rights are alleged, bring an infringement/opposition action before the tribunal judiciaire or INPI as applicable. If the refusal relates to a regulated token, the prior ministerial or prudential approval must be obtained and attached to the application. Refusal decisions stating legal grounds are subject to judicial review.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for registered office purposes only. A French SARL may use an approved domiciliation provider under Article L.123-11-2 and R.123-166 et seq. of the French Commercial Code. However, ISIC 2720 sodium-ion battery cell manufacturing requires a physical operating and warehousing facility for environmental (ICPE) classification, product safety approvals and commercial substance; a virtual office alone will not support the required manufacturing license.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High – approximately 70% within the first 24 months of obtaining the operational permit. DREAL and other competent authorities may conduct unannounced on-site inspections of manufacturing premises under environmental and industrial safety regulations.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce (Law no. 2000-1208 of 22 December 2000), articles L. 223-1 to L. 223-47
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) administered by the greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte de constitution et statuts de la société
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum subscribed capital of 1 EUR; no escrow account required
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The first Board of Directors of the proposed Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL) convened to resolve the following: 1. Subscription to the initial share capital amounting to one thousand euros (1,000 EUR) by the sole shareholder. 2. Adoption of the registered office located at [full address in France]. 3. Appointment of [Director Name] as Président and [Manager Name] as gérant. 4. Authorization for the filing of the acte de constitution and statuts with the greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, publication in the Journal Officiel, and all subsequent administrative formalities. 5. Confirmation of compliance with the Code de commerce and all applicable French corporate laws. This resolution was adopted unanimously on [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Drafting of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a French notary to draft the acte de constitution and statuts. Provide all required documents including ID, address, capital details, and shareholder information. Notary will verify and sign the documents.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If queried, provide additional clarifications or amend the draft within 48 hours

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the signed documents to the notary for authentication. Pay the notarization fee. Obtain certified copies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized acte de constitution and statuts to the greffe. Pay filing fees. The greffe will issue the SIREN and SIRET numbers. Publication in Journal Officiel will follow.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If application queried, submit additional documents or respond to observations within the prescribed period

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle) online portal

step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If rejected, appeal to the tribunal within 2 days

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP); official portal impots.gouv.fr; company registration formalities via the Guichet Unique at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign parent incorporating a French SARL files the statutory dossier through the Guichet Unique (one-stop e-registration). The Guichet automatically issues the SIREN/SIRET identifiers and coordinates with DGFiP for the French intra-community VAT number (TVA intracommunautaire). After validation, the SARL holds a corporate tax identification number based on its SIREN and a VAT ID configured under the 'FR' prefix, verifiable through the EU VIES portal. For customs and excise purposes, the same EORI number is granted.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL) is subject to French corporate income tax at the entity level, with full tax residence in France. French resident companies are taxable on worldwide profits, with the exception of permanent establishment profits that may be exempted under treaty provisions. Tax-exempt zone status is not automatic.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France has no check-the-box regime. Statutory elections include: (i) option for income-tax treatment (impôt sur le revenu) under CG I Art. 239 bis AA for eligible family-owned SARLs and certain small companies; (ii) election for French fiscal integration (intégration fiscale) for French-parent groups holding at least 95% direct/indirect subsidiaries; (iii) ATAD-compliant hybrid mismatch elections are not elective; adjustments apply automatically under CGI Art. 212 bis and 212 bis A where mismatches arise.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For established French taxable persons, the franchise en base threshold applies: EUR 85,000 annual sales of goods and EUR 34,400 annual sales of services. Non-established foreign suppliers must register for French VAT from the first taxable supply unless a special non-EU or EU scheme applies. Manufacturing of sodium-ion battery cells as goods is therefore captured by the goods-related threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France mandates electronic invoicing for all B2B domestic supplies through the public invoicing portal (PPF) or certified dematerialization platforms (PDPs). The PPP/PDP mandate is phased: large and mid-size enterprises from 1 September 2026, small and micro enterprises from 1 September 2027. E-reporting to DGFiP is required for B2C and cross-border supplies. Invoices must use structured formats (Factur-X/UBL). There is no per-transaction real-time clearance or digital fiscal stamping in France.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (exemption with input VAT deduction) applies to sodium-ion battery cells sold for export outside the European Union, provided the goods are physically dispatched or transported out of the EU by the seller, purchaser, or a third party for their account. Eligibility requires proof of the transfer of ownership, payment consideration, and evidence that the goods left EU customs territory. For intra-community supplies, the customer's valid EU VAT ID is required; injury or non-collection may result in recharacterisation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU/SAD lodged via the French customs system, currently DELTA/D providers).
Bill of Lading (or CMR/air waybill) evidencing physical movement outside the EU.
Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign-exchange bank proof confirming actual payment proceeds.
Commercial invoice, purchase order, delivery note, and customs export summary declaration.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP and French Customs may apply intensified audit scrutiny to export zero-rating claims. If zero-rating is erroneously applied or evidence proves fraudulent, the VAT is retroactively clawed back at 20% plus monthly late-interest of 0.67%. Penalties range from 40% for negligent under-declaration to 80% for deliberate bad faith, increasing further for abuse of law or tax evasion. Criminal fines apply under CGI Art. 1741 up to EUR 300,000 with imprisonment up to seven years; the limitation period for tax recovery is extended to ten years in cases of fraud or fictitious exports.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), together with the French Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority (ACPR) and the French Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty for exchange-control policy and balance-of-payments reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a euro-zone member and applies full current-account and capital-account convertibility under EU Treaty liberalisation. No general exchange controls or prior authorizations apply to cross-border payments. Inbound foreign direct investments above €750,000 trigger ex-post balance-of-payments reporting to the Banque de France (direct investment survey). Profit remittances, dividends, and loan reimbursements by a French SARL are unrestricted after applicable corporate tax and social charges, subject to standard corporate formalities, withholding tax treaty treatment where applicable, and AML/KYC verification by the paying bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender requirement, forced conversion, or minimum retention rule for export receipts under French or EU law. Exporters may freely hold proceeds in euros or foreign currency. All merchandise trade settlements must be reported to the Banque de France for statistical purposes within 12 working days following the transaction or declaration threshold trigger, but the currency of settlement and conversion timing remain entirely at the discretion of the exporter.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Corporate Treasury and FX Hedging Account
Operational Account and Trade Finance Line
Operational Account for Regional SME Support

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-High for ancillary payment services and FX conversion, subject to a key legal constraint: EU Payment Institutions / Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) must be ACPR-licensed and EU-established under PSD2. They cannot hold client funds on balance sheet, cannot provide commercial loans, letters of credit, or regulated escrow services, and their suitability for large-capital injections or asset-backed treasury operations is limited. EMIs such as Qonto, Shine, or Wise are acceptable for day-to-day supplier payments, payroll, and small-to-mid-sized FX toroidal flows, but the primary settlement and treasury clearing rails must be tier-1 licensed banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a French SARL with non-resident shareholders and a manufacturing profile in batteries, most tier-1 banks mandate at least one manager and the ultimate beneficial owner to attend an in-person KYC/ADR interview at the bank branch, or at a recognized notary/consulate where the durable power is executed. Pure remote opening is rarely offered by major commercial banks for medium-risk, cross-border manufacturing entities. Selected ACPR-licensed fintechs provide 100% remote onboarding, but they usually require biometric identity verification, apostilled corporate documents, a certified French translation of foreign registry excerpts, and a video-recorded Q&A session. A statutory domiciliation address and a French tax number (SIRET) remain mandatory in all cases.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large initial paid-in capital originating from low- or non-transparent offshore jurisdictions prior to revenue generation, creating a source-of-funds and source-of-wealth red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized share subscription agreements; audited or management-prepared business plan; bank statements of the contributing shareholder or lender covering at least the preceding 12 months; SWIFT MT103 confirmation of each inbound contribution; French Kbis extraction; formal declaration of the identity of the ultimate beneficial owner; and tax residence certificates of the investor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sector scrutiny over advanced battery-cell manufacturing and possible dual-use / sensitive technology transfer classification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ISIC 2720 and NAICS 335911 classification letter from a certified legal counsel; technical data sheet and product specification demonstrating the sodium-ion cell chemistry is designed exclusively for micro-mobility (e-bikes, scooters, low-voltage vehicles); end-use certificate from end customers; EU dual-use list review certificate (Regulation (EU) 2021/821) confirming non-controlled status; and ISO 9001 / environmental compliance attestations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex beneficial shareholding structure involving multiple EU and overseas corporate layers, obscuring ultimate control.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group structure chart down to the individual controller; French register of beneficial owners (RBE) submission receipt; notarized partnership agreements or share transfer register; passport copies of controllers; good-standing certificates from each corporate jurisdiction; and a written KYC ownership narrative explaining control and economic purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: A high volume of outbound trade disbursements to non-EU suppliers in countries of heightened money-laundering or sanctions risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trade package per shipment: pro-forma and commercial invoices, packing list, bill of lading / AWB, letter of credit terms, intercompany or supplier master agreement, counterparty KYB questionnaire, and sanctions screening output from an automated compliance tool; all files shall be made available to the French bank upon request.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential misclassification of capital escrow versus operational flows, causing confusion over transaction purpose codes and AML monitoring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed treasury mandate manual containing the authorized signatories, purpose-code mapping for each account (foreign direct investment, trade settlement, operational expenses), flow-specific legal backups, internal authorisation matrix, and contemporaneous minutes of the SARL manager or shareholders' meeting approving each treasury operation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound funds for paid-in capital or shareholder loans must be routed via SWIFT MT103 (or TARGET2 / SEPA for EUR-denominated transfers) to the beneficiary SARL IBAN. Crucial compliance elements: a correct transaction purpose code (e.g., 'C10 - equity acquisition', 'C25 - shareholder loan', or 'D20 - other investment'), a unique end-to-end transaction reference (UETR), pre-notification to the receiving bank in the prescribed KYC form, and a full economic rationale accompanied by notarized corporate resolutions. The financing bank must submit the balance-of-payments declaration to the Banque de France when the direct investment threshold or the €750,000 declaration rule is met. Where the contribution is non-cash (e.g., machinery for the sodium-ion production line), an independent valuer report and notarized contribution deed are required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements are executed primarily through SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier payments and confirmed or unconfirmed documentary Letters of Credit (L/C) for capital equipment, raw magnesium or sodium-ion precursor purchases, and large-scale international deliveries. French banks may advise or confirm L/Cs via R-FBC (Règlement Financier Bancaire de Crédit) and will condition non-recourse or discounting on clean presentation. For intra-EU supplier payments, SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) in EUR is the standard low-cost rail, while SWIFT is mandatory for third-country currencies. All outbound flows must be matched to the correct invoice, customs declaration (Déclaration d'Échanges de Biens), and export exoneration code, and must align with Incoterms 2020.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot FX conversion for EUR/USD, EUR/CNY and major trade currencies
Outright FX forwards (maturity up to 12-14 months) for known trade receivables and payables
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) covering emerging-market currencies where no onshore deliverable market is accessible
Cross-currency swaps for multi-year capital equipment financing
FX swaps and tom/next swaps for temporary liquidity bridging between currency accounts
FX options (call/put) with underlying commercial exposure, subject to bank credit-line approval
Currency-collateralized money-market instruments for hedging counterparty exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return — liasse fiscale (n°2065-SD and annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP (Direction Générale des Finances Publiques) via electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December fiscal year, due by the second business day after 1 May of the following year; for non-calendar-year closings, generally due within six months of the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% to 10% of assessed tax, increasing to 40% for bad faith and 80% for fraud, plus monthly late-payment interest at 0.40%; persistent failure may trigger enforced collection and tax assessment procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual approval of financial statements by the shareholders' ordinary general meeting (AGO)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate organ; decision recorded in the company's minute book at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the fiscal year-end; for a 31 December year-end, no later than 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The manager may be held civilly liable for loss caused by late approval; a shareholder may petition the court to order the meeting; failure to then file accounts within the statutory window triggers registry strike-off risk.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual financial statements and statutory reports with the commercial registry (dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Registry) in the district of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the shareholders' approval of the annual accounts; for approval on 30 June, filing is due by 31 July (calendar month computation applies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing triggers a civil fine up to EUR 15,000 against the legal representative, judicial penalty payments (astreinte), and, after formal notice and continued non-compliance, possible court-ordered strike-off (radiation) from the registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual economic contribution declarations — CVAE annual return (n°1330-CVAE-SD) and CFE balance declaration/payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP (Service des Impôts des Entreprises of the principal place of business)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: CVAE annual return due by the second business day after 1 May of the year following the tax period; CFE final payment due by 15 December of the assessment year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late declaration or payment exposes the company to late-filing penalties, 10% increase for late or omitted payment after the due date, and ongoing monthly interest at 0.20%; non-compliance may lead to enforced tax recovery.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit of a French SARL applies when, at the end of a financial year, at least two of the following three thresholds are exceeded: balance-sheet total above EUR 4,000,000; net turnover excluding VAT above EUR 8,000,000; average permanent employees above 50. Audit may also be required on demand by shareholders representing at least one-tenth of capital or under consolidation rules in a parent group.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Private French SARL must apply French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général) as implemented by the Code de commerce and ANC regulations; IFRS/EU-IFRS applies only to listed and consolidated entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: French law does not require a standalone annual UBO return. The SARL must file a beneficial-owner declaration initially and within 30 days of any transfer of shares or change of beneficial ownership. At the time of the annual accounts approval, management must verify the accuracy of the UBO information in the RCS and immediately file an update if a change has not yet been declared; omission exposes the company to a EUR 7,500 fine and the manager to possible criminal penalties.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Decisions and Minutes (Registre des procès-verbaux et des décisions collectives)
Attendance Register for Annual General Meetings (Registre de présence)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 160 - 650 per year for standard French registered-office domiciliation or corporate agent services; premium Paris business centre addresses range up to USD 1,000
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,500 - 17,500 for a compact SARL statutory audit where the audit thresholds are crossed; larger enterprises with complex manufacturing inventory and international sales typically exceed USD 20,000

tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 3 months after the end of the fiscal year (e.g., 31 March for calendar year 2023 companies)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: N/A - applies to French tax residents only

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions for R&D expenses, donations to associations, and other eligible items

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 0.75% of the tax due per month of delay, capped at 10% of the tax due, plus interest on late payments at the official rate

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% (no withholding tax on dividends distributed by French SARL to shareholders)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Obtain Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from French tax authorities and submit with relevant declaration to claim DTA benefits if parent is in a treaty country
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% to 10% depending on treaty (e.g., 0% under many EU treaties); Interest: 0% to 10% (e.g., 0% under EU Savings Directive equivalents)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: 50,000,000 EUR (turnover threshold for local file and master file requirements)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France adheres to OECD BEPS Action 5 and EU directives; economic substance requirements apply to holding companies and certain entities for tax residency purposes, including adequate employees, premises, and core income-generating activities

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of income or false declarations to reduce tax liability
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties including fines up to 80% of evaded tax, imprisonment up to 5 years, and restitution of evaded amounts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal criminal liability, including imprisonment and disqualification from management positions

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SARL solely for tax avoidance without genuine economic activity or substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Nullity of the company acts, backdated tax assessments, and penalties up to 500,000 EUR or more
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil leading to personal tax liability and potential criminal prosecution

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct proper due diligence or report suspicious transactions under French AML rules
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to 1 million EUR or 10% of annual turnover, plus criminal sanctions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines and imprisonment for willful non-compliance

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain TP documentation or apply arm's length principle in intra-group transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties of 100% of the tax adjustment, plus interest and potential criminal liability for fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for tax shortfalls and potential jail time for fraudulent conduct
